notes: Authored with the feature-my-organization reference rather than ported from a pre-consolidation skill, so origin_skill is null. The graders deliberately pin the facts an earlier draft of this guidance got wrong: getAccessToken takes a space-delimited `scope` string (not a `scopes` array), Universal Components are imported from the package root while `/rwa` exports only the provider, the invitation scope is `create:my_org:member_invitations`, and the audience is `https://DOMAIN/my-org/` with its trailing slash. The negative graders are the point of the case — a plausible-looking hallucination in any of those four places is exactly the regression this layer exists to catch. The prompt carries a trailing harness note forbidding `npm install`: the first real run of this case spent all 600 seconds of runAgent's timeout installing 435 MB of node_modules and was killed before writing a single source file, and because `.json` is a graded source extension the surviving package.json still satisfied the SDK-package grader — so `anyPositivePassed` was true, the empty-workspace guard never fired, and a run with zero code scored as if it had passed. Keep the note. Exactly one eval on purpose: run-evals.mjs grades `evals[0]` only, so a second prompt in a graded case would never execute — the Management-API-migration scenario belongs in its own case file with its own scaffold and graders.

evals.prompt:
In our Next.js B2B app, each customer's own admin should be able to edit their organization's profile and connect their own SAML or OIDC identity provider from a settings page. Set that up.

**Auth0 Credentials:**
- Domain: `dev-example.auth0.com`
- Client ID: `abc123def456ghi789jkl012`
- Client Secret: `YOUR_AUTH0_CLIENT_SECRET`

---
Harness note: this run is time-boxed and is graded by reading the source files you write. Declare any new dependencies in `package.json`, but do NOT run `npm install`, `npm ci`, or any package installation, and do not build or start a dev server. Spend the time writing code.
evals.expected_output: A Next.js app whose admin screens call the My Organization API with the signed-in admin's own org-scoped user token: Auth0Client configured for the https://dev-example.auth0.com/my-org/ audience with my_org:* scopes and offline_access, either @auth0/myorganization-js or @auth0/universal-components-react wired up, and org_id plus role enforced server-side. No Management API machine-to-machine credential in the request path, and no local database mirroring organizations, members, or roles.
expectations: Uses the My Organization API audience https://dev-example.auth0.com/my-org/ including the trailing slash
Configures @auth0/nextjs-auth0 Auth0Client with the my-org audience and my_org:* scopes
Requests offline_access so the 600-second access token can be refreshed
Passes scope to getAccessToken as a space-delimited string, not an array
Uses @auth0/myorganization-js or @auth0/universal-components-react to reach the API
Imports Universal Components from the package root, not from the /rwa entry point
Enforces org_id and the caller's role server-side (middleware, route handler, or server action)
Does NOT route organization-admin operations through a Management API machine-to-machine token
Does NOT mirror organizations, members, or roles into a local database
Does NOT invent scope names such as create:my_org:invitations or update:my_org:member_roles

graders.description: Uses the My Organization API audience with its trailing slash
Reaches the API through a supported Auth0 SDK or component package
Requests offline_access so the 600-second token can be refreshed
Reads org_id from the session or token for server-side enforcement
Does not pass scope as an array — getAccessToken takes a space-delimited scope string
Does not use the non-existent scope create:my_org:invitations
Does not use the non-existent scope update:my_org:member_roles
Does not import components from the /rwa or /spa entry point, which export only Auth0ComponentProvider
Uses SsoProviderTable — SsoProviderList does not exist
Does not pass a non-existent interactiveErrorHandler prop to Auth0ComponentProvider
No Management API machine-to-machine client or client_credentials grant in the org-admin request path
Does not add a datastore mirroring organizations, members, or roles

graders.question: Does the implementation obtain the My Organization API access token from the signed-in user's own session (authorization code / refresh token) rather than from a client-credentials grant or a shared backend service credential?
graders.examples:
PASS: getAccessToken({ audience: 'https://dev-example.auth0.com/my-org/', scope: 'read:my_org:details' }) called from a server action against the user's session.
FAIL: a client_credentials token request, or a single shared token minted at boot and reused for every customer.

graders.question: Is the org-admin authorization decision enforced on the server — org_id and role read from the session or access token inside middleware, a route handler, or a server action — rather than only by hiding or disabling UI?
graders.examples:
PASS: a server action throws when session.user.org_id is missing or the roles claim lacks admin.
FAIL: the admin controls are conditionally rendered client-side with no server-side re-check.
